panels.title: RPC Error Rate [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Percentage of each RPC command's calls that ended in an error.
**How it's computed:** Error calls divided by total calls per command over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Green below 1%, yellow 1-5%, red above 5%.
**Healthy range:** Below 1% for healthy commands.
**Watch for:** A sustained error spike on one command is consistent with a client probing or misusing that endpoint.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (command, service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (command, service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[$__rate_interval])) * 100

panels.title: Top Commands by Volume [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** The ten most-called RPC commands by total invocations recently.
**How it's computed:** Ranked total counts per command over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Identifies the hottest API endpoints driving node load.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** An unexpected command dominating the ranking can indicate scripted abuse or a misbehaving client.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (command, service_instance_id) (increase(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: WebSocket Message Rate [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of incoming WebSocket RPC messages the server processes.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Non-zero only when clients connect over WebSocket rather than HTTP.
**Healthy range:** Zero is normal for HTTP-only deployments; otherwise workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** An unexpected surge points to a chatty or abusive WebSocket client.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp:ServerHandler::processSession

panels.title: RPC Request Rate by Command
panels.description:
**What:** Per-command throughput of RPC calls the node serves (e.g. server_info, submit, account_info).
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate split by command name over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Shows which API endpoints drive load and how demand shifts over time.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; varies with client mix.
**Watch for:** A sudden spike on one command can indicate a runaway client or scripted abuse.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (command, service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: RPC Latency P95 by Command
panels.description:
**What:** 95th-percentile response time for each RPC command.
**How it's computed:** 95th percentile of per-command durations over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Read-only lookups should be fast; heavy commands like path finding are naturally slower.
**Healthy range:** Sub-second for most commands; command-dependent.
**Watch for:** Rising p95 on a normally fast command signals contention or an expensive query pattern.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, command, service_instance_id) (rate(span_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*"}[5m])))

panels.title: RPC Latency Heatmap
panels.description:
**What:** Distribution of RPC response times over time across all commands.
**How it's computed:** Counts of requests by duration band in each 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** A single tight band is healthy; brighter cells mark the common latency.
**Healthy range:** Concentrated at low latency; command-dependent.
**Watch for:** Two separate bands (bimodal latency) reveal a slow path affecting some requests.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

panels.title: Overall RPC Throughput
panels.description:
**What:** Aggregate request flow through two pipeline layers: the outer HTTP handler that accepts connections and the inner layer that parses and dispatches.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of each layer over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** The two lines should overlap when requests flow cleanly.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; both layers tracking each other.
**Watch for:** A gap means requests are being queued or rejected before dispatch.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp:ServerHandler::processSession, ServerHandler::processRequest

panels.title: RPC Success vs Error
panels.description:
**What:** Aggregate rate of successful versus failed RPC commands across all types.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of each outcome over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Success should dominate; the error line should stay low.
**Healthy range:** Error rate near zero; success rate is workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A sustained rise in the error line warrants drilling into the per-command breakdown.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", status_code="STATUS_CODE_UNSET"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", command=~"$command", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: RPC Resource Cost by Command
panels.description:
**What:** RPC traffic grouped by its resource-cost category, distinguishing cheap lookups from expensive or malformed requests.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate per cost category over a 5-minute window.
**Reading it:** Low-cost categories should dominate.
**Healthy range:** Mostly low-cost traffic; workload-dependent.
**Watch for:** A rising share of high-cost or malformed categories points to problematic or abusive clients.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/RPCHandler.cpp:callMethod

targets.expr: sum by (load_type) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name=~"rpc.command.*", load_type!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Batch vs Single RPC Requests
panels.description:
**What:** Rate of batched RPC requests versus single requests.
**How it's computed:** Per-second rate of each over a 5-minute window, per node.
**Reading it:** Most traffic is typically single requests.
**Healthy range:** Workload-dependent; batch share usually small.
**Watch for:** A high batch rate may indicate bulk-automation clients or an attempt to amplify load per connection.
**Source:** src/xrpld/rpc/detail/ServerHandler.cpp:ServerHandler::processRequest

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="rpc.process", is_batch="true"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (service_instance_id) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", span_name="rpc.process", is_batch="false"}[$__rate_interval]))
